name: AEA: bundle-affordability condition
content: AEA holds at date t if every household can afford the reference bundle b, that is, Y_{h,t}\ge P_t(b) for all h\in\mathcal{H}.

name: ATA is not sufficient in general
content: There exist economies in which increasing ATA intensity a lowers \bar{C}_t(b) and reduces rent intensity r_{\ell,t}(a) in some layers, yet AEA fails because rent intensity rises in layers with large \kappa_\ell(b) and household claims \omega_{h\ell} on those layers are sufficiently concentrated that (6) is violated for some households.

Construct an economy in which \kappa_{\ell^\ast}(b) is large for some layer \ell^\ast, in which r_{\ell^\ast,t}(a) increases with a, and in which \omega_{h\ell^\ast}=0 for a nontrivial subset of households while transfers T_{h,t} are fixed and small. Then the right-hand side of (6) rises for those households while the left-hand side does not, so AEA fails even if \bar{C}_t(b) falls.
